column1: particularity§The particularity of the account is what makes it credible: nine names, four dates, and one weather report.§这份记述的**具体入微**正是它可信之处——九个人名、四个日期，还有一份天气报告。§particul（细节，同 particle 微粒）
partisan§The report was attacked as partisan by both parties, which is roughly the best a referee can hope for.§这份报告被两党都攻击为**党派偏袒的**，这大约是仲裁者能指望的最好结果。§part（部分／党派）
partisanship§Partisanship stopped at the county line for nine years, and then a national campaign arrived.§**党派之争**在郡界外停了九年，然后一场全国竞选来了。§
passion§His passion for the subject was obvious and his grasp of it, four questions in, was not.§他对这个课题的**热情**显而易见，而问到第四个问题时，他的掌握程度就不然了。§pass（受苦，同 passive 被动的）→ 受难而生的强烈情感
passivity§The passivity of the board was the finding: nine meetings, no questions, and one signature each time.§董事会的**被动无为**正是调查结论——九次会议，零提问，每次一个签名。§
pathos§The pathos of the letters comes from their ordinariness: he writes about the weather until the last page.§这些信的**悲怆**来自它们的平常——他一直写天气，直到最后一页。§
patronage§The theatre survived on the patronage of four families and closed the year the last of them left town.§这家剧院靠四个家族的**赞助**存活，在最后一家离开小镇那年关门。§patr（父亲，同 paternal 父亲的）→ 像家长一样照拂
paucity§The paucity of records for those four years is itself evidence of how the office was run.§那四年记录的**匮乏**本身就是这个办公室如何运作的证据。§pauc（少）
pedant§The pedant on the committee was right about the comma and wrong about everything that mattered.§委员会里那个**书呆子**在逗号上是对的，在所有要紧的事上都错了。§
pedantic§The objection was pedantic in form and substantial in effect: the definition really did change the result.§这条反对意见形式上**迂腐**，效果上很实在——那个定义确实改变了结果。§
pedantry§Pedantry about terminology delayed a paper for two years, and its central claim has never since been disputed.§对术语的**卖弄学问式**纠缠把一篇论文拖了两年，而它的核心论断此后从未被质疑。§
peer§Her peers rejected the paper four times, and the field it opened now supports nine research groups.§她的**同行**四次退了这篇论文，而它开启的领域如今养着九个研究组。§par（相等，同 par 平价）
pejorative§The word is pejorative now and was purely descriptive when the statute used it in 1911.§这个词如今是**贬义的**，而 1911 年法条用它时纯属描述。§pejor（更坏）
penalty§The penalty is nine hundred pounds and the profit from breaking the rule is about forty thousand.§**罚款**是九百英镑，而违规的利润约四万。§pen（惩罚，同 punish 惩罚）
penchant§His penchant for old maps became, after nine years, the basis of a genuinely useful archive.§他对旧地图的**偏好**在九年后成了一座真正有用的档案库的基础。§
penitent§The penitent letter arrived four years late and asked for nothing, which is why the family kept it.§这封**悔过的**信迟到四年，什么也没请求，所以那家人留下了它。§penit（悔恨，同 repent 忏悔）
penurious§The penurious years taught him habits that four decades of comfort never quite undid.§那些**贫困的**年头教会他一些习惯，四十年的宽裕也没能完全改掉。§penur（贫乏）
perceptive§A perceptive reader will notice that the narrator never once describes his own face.§**敏锐的**读者会注意到叙述者一次也没描写过自己的脸。§per（完全）+ cept（拿，同 capture 捕获）→ 全接收到
perennial§Staffing is the perennial problem here, and every review since 1994 has named it first.§人手是这里**长年不断的**问题，1994 年以来每次评估都把它列在首位。§per（贯穿）+ enn（年，同 annual 每年的）
perfectionist§The perfectionist on the team shipped nothing for nine months and then shipped something flawless.§团队里那位**完美主义者**九个月什么也没交付，然后交付了一件毫无瑕疵的东西。§
perfidious§The perfidious ally signed two treaties in the same month and honoured neither of them.§这个**背信弃义的**盟友同月签了两份条约，一份也没遵守。§per（彻底）+ fid（信任，同 fidelity 忠诚）→ 把信任毁到底
perfidy§The perfidy was documented in his own diary, which his family published nine years after his death.§这桩**背信**记录在他自己的日记里，家人在他死后九年出版了它。§
perfunctory§The inspection was perfunctory: four minutes for a site that takes an hour to walk around.§这次检查是**敷衍了事的**——绕一圈要一小时的厂区，只用了四分钟。§per（完全）+ funct（履行，同 function 功能）→ 只把过场走完
periodic§The periodic review happens every four years and has recommended the same change every time since 1998.§这项**定期**评审每四年一次，自 1998 年起每次都建议同一项改动。§period（周期）
periodically§The valve is inspected periodically, which the manual defines as "whenever the plant is otherwise shut down."§这个阀门**定期**检查，而手册对此的定义是「工厂因其他原因停工时」。§
peripheral§The question looked peripheral in March and turned out to be the only one that mattered by September.§这个问题三月看着**边缘无关**，到九月却成了唯一要紧的。§peri（周围，同 perimeter 周长）
perishable§The cargo was perishable and the port strike lasted nine days, and nothing was salvaged.§这批货是**易腐的**，而港口罢工持续九天，什么也没抢救回来。§per（完全）+ ish ← ir（走，同 exit 出去）→ 彻底走掉
permissive§The rule is permissive rather than mandatory, and four of the nine councils have simply ignored it.§这条规定是**许可性的**而非强制性的，九个议会里有四个干脆无视了它。§permiss（允许，同 permit 许可）
permutation§Every permutation was tried, and the one that worked was the one the team had dismissed first.§每一种**排列**都试过了，而奏效的是团队最先排除的那一种。§per（彻底）+ mut（改变，同 mutation 突变）
pernicious§The most pernicious effect was invisible: nine years of small compromises that nobody recorded.§最**有害的**影响是看不见的——九年里无人记录的小小妥协。§per（彻底）+ nic ← noc（伤害，同 innocuous 无害的）
perpetuate§The scheme perpetuates a disadvantage it was designed to remove, and the data has shown this since 2011.§这个方案让它本要消除的劣势**长期延续**下去，数据自 2011 年起就显示了这点。§per（贯穿）+ pet（追求，同 petition 请愿）
perplex§The result perplexed four laboratories, and the explanation turned out to be a mislabelled reagent.§这个结果**困惑**了四家实验室，而解释原来是一瓶贴错标签的试剂。§per（完全）+ plex（编织，同 complex 复杂的）→ 绕成一团
perquisite§The perquisites were worth more than the salary, and neither appeared in the published figures.§这些**额外津贴**比薪水还值钱，而两者都没出现在公布的数字里。§per（彻底）+ quisit（寻求，同 require 需要）
persevere§She persevered through nine rejections, and the tenth publisher printed four editions in two years.§她**坚持**熬过九次退稿，第十家出版社两年印了四版。§per（贯穿）+ sever（严格，同 severe 严厉的）
persist§The fault persists in cold weather and disappears entirely once the temperature rises above about four degrees.§这个故障在寒冷天气里**持续存在**，气温一升到约四度以上就完全消失。§per（贯穿）+ sist（站立，同 assist 协助）
persistent§Her persistent questioning uncovered in nine months what four formal inquiries had failed to find.§她**持续不懈的**追问在九个月里查出了四次正式调查都没找到的东西。§
personality§The department's personality came almost entirely from four people who all left in the same year.§这个系的**性格**几乎全来自四个人，而他们同年都离开了。§
perspicacious§The most perspicacious remark of the evening came from someone who had said nothing for two hours.§那晚最**有洞察力的**一句话，出自一个两小时没开口的人。§per（穿透）+ spic（看，同 inspect 检查）→ 看得穿
persuasive§The argument is persuasive and the evidence is thin, which is a combination worth being careful about.§这个论证**有说服力**而证据单薄，这是值得警惕的组合。§per（彻底）+ suad（劝，同 dissuade 劝阻）
pertain§The rule pertains only to buildings put up before 1948, which is about nine percent of the stock.§这条规定只**适用于**1948 年前建的楼房，约占存量的百分之九。§per（彻底）+ tain（拿住，同 contain 容纳）
pertinent§The most pertinent question was asked last and answered, as it happened, in four words.§最**切题的**问题是最后问的，而回答恰好只用了四个词。§
perturb§Nothing perturbed him except imprecision, and a rounded figure could ruin his whole afternoon.§除了不精确，没有什么能**扰乱**他，一个约整的数字能毁掉他整个下午。§per（彻底）+ turb（搅动，同 turbulence 湍流）
peruse§She perused the contract for four hours and found the clause everyone else had skimmed past.§她**细读**了四小时合同，找出了其他人都草草掠过的那一条。§per（彻底）+ use（使用）→ 用尽了看
pervasive§The smell is pervasive rather than strong, and visitors notice it about nine minutes after arriving.§这气味是**无处不在的**而非浓烈的，访客大约在到达九分钟后才注意到。§per（贯穿）+ vas（走，同 evade 逃避）
pestilence§The pestilence of 1665 emptied four parishes, and the registers stop entirely for eleven months.§1665 年的**瘟疫**清空了四个教区，登记册整整十一个月没有记录。§pest（瘟疫，同 pest 害虫）
pettiness§The pettiness of the dispute was in inverse proportion to the number of hours spent on it.§这场争执的**琐屑**程度与花在它上面的小时数成反比。§petit（小）
petulant§His petulant response to a fair question cost him more support than the question ever could.§他对一个公允问题的**任性使气**回应，让他失去的支持超过那个问题本身。§pet（冲，同 impetuous 冲动的）
philanthropic§The philanthropic foundation gave away four million pounds and employed nine people to decide how.§这家**慈善**基金会捐出四百万英镑，雇了九个人来决定怎么捐。§phil（爱，同 philosophy 哲学）+ anthrop（人，同 anthropology 人类学）
phlegmatic§The phlegmatic captain reported the collision in the same tone he used for the weather.§这位**冷静沉着的**船长报告碰撞时用的语气与报天气一模一样。§
phobic§The phobic response is disproportionate by definition, which is what separates it from ordinary caution.§**恐惧症的**反应按定义就是不成比例的，这正是它区别于寻常谨慎之处。§
picayune§The objection was picayune in substance and it still delayed a nine-million-pound project by four whole months.§这条反对意见实质上**微不足道**，却仍把一个九百万英镑的项目整整拖了四个月。§
piety§His piety was private, and the four charities in his will were the first anyone heard of it.§他的**虔敬**是私人的，遗嘱里的四家慈善机构是人们第一次听说这件事。§pi（虔诚，同 pious 虔诚的）
pigment§The pigment was made from a mineral mined in one valley, and the colour vanished from painting when the mine closed.§这种**颜料**取自一条河谷开采的矿物，矿一关，这种颜色就从绘画中消失了。§pig ← ping（涂，同 paint 油漆）
pilfer§Someone pilfered small sums for nine years, and the total came to more than four hundred thousand.§有人**小额偷窃**了九年，总额超过四十万。§
pivotal§The pivotal moment was procedural: a motion to adjourn that four members voted against.§**关键性的**时刻是程序性的——一项休会动议，四名成员投了反对票。§pivot（枢轴）
placate§Nothing placated the crowd until the mayor came out and stood, without a microphone, for nine minutes.§直到市长走出来不用话筒站了九分钟，人群才被**安抚**下来。§plac（取悦，同 please 使高兴）
placid§The placid surface of the lake hides a current that has drowned four strong swimmers.§这片湖**平静的**水面下藏着一股水流，已淹死四名游泳好手。§plac（平静，同 placate 抚慰）
plasticity§The plasticity of the young brain is remarkable and, after about nine years, sharply reduced.§幼年大脑的**可塑性**惊人，而在约九岁后急剧下降。§plast（塑造，同 plastic 塑料）
platitude§The speech was four minutes of platitude and one sentence that told you what would actually change.§这篇讲话是四分钟的**陈词滥调**，加上一句真正说明会有什么改变的话。§plat（平坦，同 plateau 高原）→ 平淡无味的老话
plaudit§The plaudits came from people who had not read the book, and the four reviewers who had were harsher.§**喝彩**来自没读过这本书的人，而读过的四位评论者要严厉得多。§plaud（拍手，同 applaud 鼓掌）
plausibility§The plausibility of the story is exactly what should have made investigators check it harder.§这个故事的**貌似可信**，恰恰应该让调查者查得更仔细。§
plausible§The explanation is plausible and unverifiable, and four years later nobody has managed to test it.§这个解释**似乎合理**却无法验证，四年后仍没人能检验它。§plaus（鼓掌，同 applaud 鼓掌）→ 听着让人想拍手
playful§The playful tone of the first chapter is a trap, and readers who expect it to continue are badly wrong.§第一章**俏皮的**语气是个陷阱，指望它延续下去的读者大错特错。§
plenitude§A plenitude of data has not produced a decision, and the committee has met nine times.§数据的**充盈**并没有带来决定，而委员会已经开了九次会。§plen（满，同 plenty 大量）
plentiful§Water was plentiful in this valley until 1994, and four wells have failed since.§这条河谷的水在 1994 年前一直**充足**，此后已有四口井干涸。§
plethora§A plethora of guidelines has replaced the four rules that people actually used to follow.§**过多**的指南取代了人们从前真正遵守的那四条规则。§
pliant§The material is pliant when warm and brittle at anything below about four degrees.§这种材料在温暖时**柔韧**，在约四度以下则变脆。§pli（折叠，同 pliers 钳子）
plight§The plight of the four families was reported once and then dropped, and their situation has not changed.§这四个家庭的**困境**被报道过一次便无下文，而他们的处境没有改变。§
